result.topic_en: Euler describes experiments with capillary tubes for determining the fluid-friction coefficient α from the tube length or water height at which outflow begins, and derives the condition g < αl for a tube narrow enough to stop outflow.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 359
pono hunc tubum initio tam fuiſſe longum, vt nulla
aqua efflueret; deinde eius longitudo ſucceſſiue dimi-
nuatur, donec aqua effluere incipiat: qua longitudine
notata, quae ſit $=b$, cum ſit $a-(n-1)b=0$, erit
$n=\frac{a+b}{b}$; ideoque $\alpha=\frac{\alpha+b}{b}\cdot\frac{g}{l}$.
57. Idem experimentum etiam ita inſtitui pot-
eſt, vt longitudo tubi capillaris BC data aſſumatur,
quae autem tanta ſit, vt ſi minimum aquae in vas ſu-
perius infundatur, nihil effluat; tum vero continuo au-
geatur altitudo aquae in vaſe eousque, donec aqua
per tubulum capillarem effluere incipiat. Quod cum
euenerit, notetur iſta altitudo $=a$, et quia tam longi-
tudo tubuli $b$, quam eius amplitudo $gg$, iam cognita
ponitur, elicietur vt ante $\alpha=\frac{a+b}{b}\cdot\frac{g}{l}$.
58. Perſpicuum autem eſt, tubulum, quo vti
volumus, tam arctum eſſe debere, vt ſit $g<\alpha l$; ſi
enim fuerit $g>\alpha l$, hic caſus nunquam vſu veniet, vt
effluxus aquae impediatur. Quodſi ergo ſit, vti ſuſpicari
licuit, $\alpha=\frac{1}{4000}$, ob $l=30$ ped. deberet eſſe $g>\frac{3}{400}$ ped.
ſeu $g<0,0075$ ped. ſicque diameter tubuli minor eſſe
deberet, quam $\frac{85}{10000}$ ped. ſeu quam $\frac{1}{118}$ ped. Hinc
limes, infra quem diameter tubuli capi deberet, eſſet
circiter vnius lineae.
59. Si fuerit $g=\alpha l$, ſeu $g<\alpha l$, et $a=0$,
tum ſi eiusmodi tubulus, cuiuscunque fuerit longitudinis,
aqua impleatur, nihil ex eo effluet, etiamſi in ſitu ver-
ticali detineatur. Hinc cum $l$ ſit longitudo 30 pedum,
facile per experimenta valor litterae $\alpha$ explorari pote-
rit. Parentur ſcilicet plures tubuli, quorum amplitudi-

items.quote:
Perſpicuum autem eſt, tubulum, quo vti
volumus, tam arctum eſſe debere, vt ſit $g<\alpha l$; ſi
enim fuerit $g>\alpha l$, hic caſus nunquam vſu veniet, vt
effluxus aquae impediatur.
items.english: It is clear that the tube we wish to use must be so narrow that g < αl; for if g > αl, the case in which the outflow of water is prevented will never occur.

items.quote:
Quodſi ergo ſit, vti ſuſpicari
licuit, $\alpha=\frac{1}{4000}$
items.english: If therefore, as could be suspected, α = 1/4000.

items.quote:
Hinc
limes, infra quem diameter tubuli capi deberet, eſſet
circiter vnius lineae.
items.english: Hence the limit below which the diameter of the tube would have to be taken would be about one line.

items.quote:
Hinc cum $l$ ſit longitudo 30 pedum,
facile per experimenta valor litterae $\alpha$ explorari pote-
rit.
items.english: Hence, since l is a length of 30 feet, the value of the letter α can easily be determined by experiments.
